Package org.uma.evolver.meta.problem

Class ConstrainedIndicatorValue

java.lang.Object
org.uma.evolver.meta.problem.ConstrainedIndicatorValue
public final class ConstrainedIndicatorValue extends Object
The value of a quality indicator for a configuration on a training set with constraints: a scheme of Evolver that takes the idea of the indicator of Vodopija, Tušar and Filipič ("Characterization of Constrained Continuous Multiobjective Optimization Problems: A Performance Space Perspective", IEEE TEVC 29(1), 2025), a threshold that separates feasible from infeasible results, to several runs and problems: a feasible result is always better than an infeasible one, and infeasible results are graded by their constraint violation.

Over the runs of a configuration on all the problems, the value of an indicator is 6k + 2v + Q, where

  • k is the number of runs whose result has no feasible solution: each one adds 6, more than the other two terms together, so a configuration with fewer such runs is always better;
  • v is the mean scaled violation of those runs (see scaledViolation(double, double)), in [0, 1): with the same number of failed runs, the one closer to the feasible region is better;
  • Q is the mean over the problems of the median of the indicator over their feasible runs, kept in [τ* - 2, τ*] with τ* the threshold(org.uma.jmetal.qualityindicator.QualityIndicator) of the indicator (see bounded(double, org.uma.jmetal.qualityindicator.QualityIndicator)), which is also the value of a problem without feasible runs: the quality, which only decides when the rest tie.

The indicator of Vodopija et al. itself, ConstrainedMultiobjectiveIndicator (ICMOP), can be one of the indicators: its value on the feasible solutions of a run is in [-1, τ*], so it fits in the same scheme.

With a single problem and run, this orders results as the indicator of Vodopija et al.: a feasible result below the threshold, an infeasible one above it.

    The value of an indicator on the feasible solutions of a run, kept in [τ* - 2, τ*]: capped at its threshold, as in the indicator of Vodopija et al., and bounded below so that the quality cannot outweigh a failed run (only an NHV below -1, a front with twice the hypervolume of the reference front, reaches that bound).

  • Method Details

    • threshold

      public static double threshold(org.uma.jmetal.qualityindicator.QualityIndicator indicator)
      The threshold τ* of an indicator: its worst sensible value on fronts normalized with the bounds of the reference front, at which its values are capped and which a problem without feasible runs takes.
      Parameters:
      indicator - the indicator
      Returns:
      0 for HV- (no hypervolume), 1 for NHV, EP, IGD+, Spread and GeneralizedSpread, and the threshold of ICMOP (1 by default)
      Throws:
      org.uma.jmetal.util.errorchecking.JMetalException - for an indicator without a known threshold

    • bounded

      public static double bounded(double value, org.uma.jmetal.qualityindicator.QualityIndicator indicator)
      The value of an indicator on the feasible solutions of a run, kept in [τ* - 2, τ*]: capped at its threshold, as in the indicator of Vodopija et al., and bounded below so that the quality cannot outweigh a failed run (only an NHV below -1, a front with twice the hypervolume of the reference front, reaches that bound).
      Parameters:
      value - the value of the indicator
      indicator - the indicator
      Returns:
      the value in [τ* - 2, τ*]

    • scale

      public static double scale(double[] violations)
      The scale of the constraint violation of a problem, after Vodopija et al.: the power of ten above the median violation of a sample of solutions, so that violations of problems of different magnitudes become comparable.
      Parameters:
      violations - the (non-negative) violations of a sample of solutions of the problem
      Returns:
      10^ceil(log10(median)), or 1 if the median is 0

    • scaledViolation

      public static double scaledViolation(double violation, double scale)
      A violation divided by the scale of its problem and mapped to [0, 1), so that the large violations of some problems do not dominate the mean over runs.
      Parameters:
      violation - the (non-negative) violation
      scale - the scale of the problem (see scale(double[]))
      Returns:
      x / (1 + x) with x = violation / scale

    • value

      public static double value(int failedRuns, double sumOfScaledViolations, double quality)
      The value of an indicator for a configuration.
      Parameters:
      failedRuns - the number of runs whose result has no feasible solution
      sumOfScaledViolations - the sum of the scaled violations of those runs
      quality - the mean over the problems of the capped median of the indicator over their feasible runs (the threshold for a problem without them)
      Returns:
      6k + 2v + Q
